accuracy.evidence: Every word used was checked against the English Appendix 1 common exception word lists: Year 1 (said, was, were, come, some, love, friend, school, put, push, pull) and Year 2 (door, eye, could, should, would, because, pretty, any, many, people). Spelling the days of the week is a Year 1 statutory requirement. The sound-it-out spellings (skool, luv, meny, shud, wer, becos, frend, cud, enny, peepul) are the documented phonically plausible errors, and the Wednesday etymology (Woden's day, Old English Wōdnesdæg) was checked against the Oxford English Dictionary entry.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text: spelling by sound alone (step 1 swaps, step 4 sentences, challenge 'sound' feedback), dropping a silent letter (Wensday, cud: step 3 Wens tile, challenge 'silent'), right letters in the wrong order (siad, freind: practice p1, m8, challenge 'order'), thinking the whole word is irregular (step 1 prediction 'All of it'), and copying once instead of spaced practice (m4, challenge 'once').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagexcept is built on this topic's own mechanism: a sounded-out spelling split into chunks where only one chunk is swapped for the exception grapheme (skool + ch = school), a real look-cover-write-check cycle where the word is hidden before the letter tiles appear, and the seven day names built from their tricky starts plus the regular 'day'. The reading lab flagsight marks a tricky part with a heart and flashes words; it has no covering, no swap and no days. lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers that only one part is wrong by trying it: dropping ch on the s returns 's is spelt the way it sounds, so it stays. The tricky part is k: school uses ch.' In step 2 the word disappears after Cover it, so it must be recalled, and tapping the sound-it-out letter u in come returns 'u is how it sounds, like cum. But come is a tricky word. Next comes o.' The done screens list skool → school and come ✓ (not cum).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each hold a tempting wrong answer the lab then disproves: that all of skool is wrong (step 1 shows only k changes), that come can be spelt by sounding out c, u, m (step 2 rejects the u tile), and that you can hear the d in Wednesday (step 3 shows Wensday as the sound-it-out trap).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; each wrong option carries its own message: 'sound' (spelt as it sounds), 'vowel' (schol misses oo), 'order' (siad, Wendsday: right letters, wrong order), 'silent' (cood, Wensday: the d and the l are written but not heard), 'homo' (wood sounds like would but is a different word), 'family' (some has o-says-u, not ould) and 'once' (practise on another day).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use one-syllable words and sentences of 3 to 12 words ('Say said. It sounds like sed. But we write s, a, i, d.'). Lab banners were shortened to 'Word 1 of 5: fix the tricky part' after the 360 px screenshot showed the longer text shrinking. validate_lessons readability passed (kid and adult within the limits).

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence gives a rule or an example; adult paragraphs give the statutory word lists, the one-tricky-part idea and the Wednesday history, the named mistakes, and what each lab step does. The content gate found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% the same as any other lesson, including Reading high-frequency words by sight.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 x 640 screenshots in light and dark themes for all six steps: letter tiles and day tiles are at least 48 px, the five-word sentence wraps onto three rows without clipping, the two family boxes fit side by side, and the button pad below the canvas wraps (young class gives 56 px buttons). The walkthrough also passed on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a matching button (chunk buttons labelled 'Put ch in place of k', letter buttons, day buttons, word buttons, family buttons); the canvas aria-label is updated with every feedback message; the challenge uses a role=status live region; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme on desktop and iPhone 13.
